rowSemantics: A row's coverage describes how completely that metric's source was enumerated; it does not promise a value. usage.inputTokens is coverage complete and still null with reason insufficient_data, which is not zero.
Row identity is metricId + layer + currency, so one metric can appear once per layer and once per currency and never merged. Counts print as bare numbers with the unit reported separately.
Absent components are reported per row (timing_missing, endpoint_missing, insufficient_data, no_observations); nothing is filled in from a price table, a subscription assumption or another row.
review.activeMs is a partial UI-visibility proxy even when the whole source enumerates completely; it is not human working time.
mainFindings: The coordinator's header coverageState folds any partial row into partial, so a completely enumerated source is served as partial. G keeps source coverage and row coverage separate in its own projection; main may prefer the header to describe enumeration only. Reported in wave28 and still observable at c5e428a2; G did not change main.

The coordinator builds display metric ids as metricId@layer@currency and leaves a trailing separator when the currency is empty (e.g. outcomes.count@controlled@), while G's row ids stop at the last present segment (outcomes.count@controlled). Consumers keyed on the exact string differ; G tolerates both by prefix matching in its own cases and does not edit the DTO.
